articles.title: Acompanhe o 1º turno das eleições no Sul de Minas
articles.summary: No g1, você acompanha a cobertura completa e a apuração dos resultados em tempo real
articles.body:
No g1, você acompanha a cobertura completa e a apuração dos resultados em tempo real

💼 Trabalhar nas eleições dá direito a folga?

Quem atua como mesário tem direito a dois dias de folga para cada dia trabalhado nas eleições, sem desconto no salário. O treinamento também garante dois dias de folga. Saiba tudo sobre!

Duas urnas eletrônicas precisaram ser substituídas durante a manhã deste domingo (4) na área da 227ª Zona Eleitoral, em Pouso Alegre. Uma delas apresentou problemas na tela na Escola Profissional Delfim Moreira, em Pouso Alegre. A outra foi trocada em Borda da Mata. Segundo o Cartório Eleitoral, a votação seguiu normalmente após as substituições.

A zona eleitoral atende cinco municípios e reúne 141.857 eleitores. Ao todo, são 475 urnas preparadas para 456 seções em 61 locais de votação.

Cidades do Sul de Minas registram ausências de mesários durante o domingo de votação.

Para votar nas eleições de 2026, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto aos mesários. O título de eleitor em papel não é obrigatório.

Também é possível votar usando apenas o aplicativo e-Título , desde que ele exiba a fotografia do eleitor. Caso a versão digital não tenha foto, será necessário apresentar outro documento oficial com foto.

Em Passos, a manhã foi de grande movimentação na E.E. Prof.ª Júlia Kubitschek, local que concentra o maior número de eleitores da cidade, com 4,5 mil pessoas.

A eleição na cidade transcorre com poucas ocorrências. Uma mulher foi detida e levada para a delegacia por boca de urna na E.E. Abraham Lincoln.

Segundo o Cartório Eleitoral de Passos, os maiores problemas foram relacionados à ausência de mesários: 16 faltaram e foram substituídos. Duas urnas precisaram ser trocadas e, após a substituição do equipamento, a votação seguiu normalmente.

Longas filas são registradas na Unifenas, em Varginha, com eleitores relatando demora para conseguir votar.

É possível levar uma cola já com a ordem de votação na urna para ajudar o eleitor ao fazer suas escolhas. No entanto, esta cola deve ser de papel. Não é permitido usar celular na cabine de votação e este deve ficar no local indicado pelos mesários enquanto o eleitor vota.

Pai e filha foram votar juntos na Faculdade Católica de Pouso Alegre (MG), no bairro Árvore Grande, por volta das 12h. O eletricista aposentado, Geraldo Soares, de 86 anos, conta que nunca deixou de votar, mesmo após não ser mais obrigatório.

"Votar é muito essencial. As nossas vidas dependem do voto".

A filha dele, Rose Soares, que é engenheira de segurança do trabalho e perita judicial, o acompanhou e reconheceu a atitude do pai.

"É uma emoção forte. Eu acho magnífico meu pai ter essa preocupação", afirmou.

Eleitores encontram enormes filas e reclamam da demora para votar na Escola Estadual Coronel Carneiro Júnior, em Itajubá.

🗳️ No 1º turno, o eleitor deverá seguir a seguinte ordem de votação: primeiro, deputado federal (4 dígitos); depois, deputado estadual (5 dígitos). Em seguida, serão escolhidos os dois senadores , com 3 dígitos para cada vaga. Na sequência, é a vez do governador (2 dígitos) e, por fim, do presidente da República (2 dígitos).

👤 Para ajudar o eleitor a consultar os candidatos de cada cargo, o g1 preparou uma ferramenta de busca que permite pesquisar por nome, partido, número e estado. Acesse aqui e confira!

📍 O g1 Sul de Minas acompanha, ao longo de todo o domingo, a movimentação nos locais de votação, as principais ocorrências e as histórias que marcam o primeiro turno das eleições na região. Veja os destaques!

A Escola Municipal Santinha Sales Gontijo, no Bairro Centenário, em Varginha, registra grande movimento de eleitores e filas na hora do almoço.

🗳️ Não vai conseguir votar? Então precisa justificar a ausência, é obrigatório. O procedimento pode ser feito sem sair de casa, basta acessar os canais oficiais da Justiça Eleitoral, como o aplicativo e-Título e o Autoatendimento Eleitoral. Clique aqui e veja como.

Ao fim da votação, o g1 Sul de Minas irá fazer a apuração das urnas em tempo real nas 162 cidades da área de cobertura. Será possível acompanhar a evolução da votação dos candidatos a presidente da República, governadores, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais.

Eleição está sendo marcada por filas e sujeira. A frente da Escola Estadual Neca Quirino, em Passos, foi tomada por santinhos de candidatos.

A gestora pública Liliane das Merces Santos se assustou com o tamanho da fila em sua seção de votação no Instituto Gammon, em Lavras, e desistiu de votar. Ela pretende voltar mais tarde.

"Tá bem cheio, acho que todo mundo pensou igual a mim, deixou para votar na hora do almoço, achando que estaria vazio, mas eu volto mais tarde para exercer meu direito de cidadã", disse.

Para a eleitora de Pouso Alegre, Leila Ferreira de Oliveira, de 52 anos, votar é importante para garantir o futuro dos seus filhos e netos. Ela disse que procura saber muito bem sobre os candidatos em que vota e fugir das fake news.

"O que plantamos hoje vai ser herança dos nossos filhos, dos nossos netos. Tem que saber os princípios dos candidatos, pois muitas vezes não estaremos mais aqui e eles vão governar para os nossos filhos e netos."

articles.title: More than 300 objections filed as Maidstone residents oppose plans to convert former Grange Moor Hotel into 42 studio apartments for 65 people, warning of added pressure on parking and infrastructure
articles.summary: Residents in Maidstone, Kent, have voiced strong opposition to plans to convert a former hotel and wedding venue into a 42-unit co-living development,
articles.body: Residents in Maidstone, Kent, have voiced strong opposition to plans to convert a former hotel and wedding venue into a 42-unit co-living development, saying they fear the proposal could put additional pressure on parking, local infrastructure and the character of the neighbourhood.More than 300 objections were submitted before the consultation deadline on September 22, with a planning decision expected at a later date.The former Grange Moor Hotel is proposed to be converted into 42 studio apartments, which could accommodate an estimated 65 people.Residents living on surrounding roads have described themselves as “devastated” by the plans, with some saying they would not have purchased their homes had they known about the proposed development, according to SWNS.‘This was our dream home’Kate Broom, 51, bought her house in May and said she would have reconsidered the purchase had she known about the proposal.“We are absolutely devastated. This was our dream home,” she said.Broom said her concerns were primarily about the scale of the proposed accommodation and the existing pressure on local services.“We have no problem with migrants. We have to house them somewhere. It is not who is going to be there, it is the volume,” she said.“It is already stressful parking, the roads are really busy. We haven’t been able to get a place at a GP surgery yet. This street can’t cope.”She added, “We definitely wouldn’t have bought this if we knew.”Former hotel was a long-standing community venueThe three-star Grange Moor Hotel underwent refurbishment and was rebranded as the Apartell in January last year. However, it closed permanently in December, with planning documents citing “major financial viability issues”.For many residents, the building had been a familiar part of the community for decades.Jake King, 38, who lives nearby with his partner and their two young children, said the proposed change was particularly upsetting because of the hotel's long history in the area.“Grange Moor has been there since I was a kid so it has always been around. To see it repurposed is sad,” he said.King said he was also concerned about how the development could affect families living nearby.“My ten-year-old son heard about it on the way to school and said he is worried about walking to school alone,” he said.Residents raise concerns over parking and property valuesJackie Farrington, 84, a former foster carer who has lived on the street for 45 years, said she was concerned about parking, crime and the potential impact on property values.“I am worried about parking and crime. We don’t know who is going to be in there. I think it will make the house value go down as well,” she said.Farrington said she had witnessed an increase in HMOs in the area and felt the character of the street had changed.“It was a lovely road but it has really changed,” she said.Yvonne Whitehead, 78, who has lived in the area for 35 years and previously ran a nearby nursing home, said the former hotel had personal significance for her family.“It used to be a lovely hotel. I used to go there for nice dinners. My children got married there,” she said.She also raised concerns about the impact of the development on local families and children.Plans include communal facilities and private parkingThe proposed development would feature 42 co-living studio apartments, along with communal kitchens, workspaces, a gym, a community living area, laundry facilities and communal gardens.The plans also include private parking spaces with electric vehicle charging facilities.Residents have speculated that the accommodation could eventually house asylum seekers, but this has not been confirmed.The concerns come amid wider complaints from some Maidstone residents about the number of HMOs being developed in the town.More HMOs planned in other parts of MaidstoneResidents in other parts of Maidstone have also raised concerns about HMO developments.Stefan, 45, who has lived on Campbell Road for five years, said several HMOs were currently being built nearby.“The main issue is overcrowding. It has changed a lot since we moved in,” he said.He also claimed that crime had increased on the street and said the frequent change of occupants was a concern.On neighbouring Rawdon Road, resident Neaveen Katta, 43, said the number of HMOs had increased significantly since she moved to the area five years ago.“There are so many HMOs. It is very difficult here,” she said, adding that she had complained to the council.Katta said she planned to move after her daughter completed her education.Planning decision yet to be madeThe consultation period for the Grange Moor Hotel proposal closed on September 22 after more than 300 objections were submitted.The objections reflect residents’ concerns about parking, infrastructure, the number of occupants and the potential impact on the surrounding community. However, the planning application remains under consideration, and a final decision has not yet been made.The proposed redevelopment would transform a former hotel and wedding venue that had served the Maidstone community for decades into a dedicated co-living scheme, making it a closely watched planning issue for residents in the surrounding neighbourhood.You use AI every day. articles.title: Baltimore shooting: 12-year-old girl killed in crossfire after parking dispute
articles.summary: A 12-year-old girl was killed after being caught in the crossfire between two men who allegedly opened fire during an argument over a parking space at a
articles.body: A 12-year-old girl was killed after being caught in the crossfire between two men who allegedly opened fire during an argument over a parking space at a Baltimore park where a youth football game was being played.Officers responded to Leon Day Park around 6:15 pm on Saturday after reports of a shooting. The girl and a woman were found with gunshot wounds, while two men involved in the incident later went to nearby hospitals seeking treatment, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said at a news conference.The girl was taken to a hospital, where she was pronounced dead. The woman and the two men suffered non-life-threatening injuries, Worley said, according to The Associated Press.Police said the shooting began after two men got into an argument, apparently over a parking space, and began firing at each other. The girl and the woman were struck by bullets.Worley said the girl was not the intended target and that police were searching for “at least” two suspects.“What we know is there was some type of argument between two cowards,” Worley said. “They both opened fire on each other. In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl, who was probably down there watching football, was shot and killed.”Police continued to process the crime scene at the expansive park and had not immediately determined how many shots were fired. Worley urged anyone who witnessed the shooting to come forward.Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott condemned the shooting and said a dispute between two adults had resulted in the death of a child.“Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone,” Scott said at the news conference. “We never should have to say something like that. What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen in my life.” Police said the investigation was ongoing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Retail store fined Rs 10k for selling expired Rs 75 mosquito repellant
articles.summary: District Consumer Commission fined a retail chain ₹10,000 for selling an expired ₹75 mosquito gel in Ludhiana, ordered refund and warned ₹200/day delay penalty.
articles.body: Ludhiana: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has penalised a retail chain store, ordering it to refund ₹75 for an expired mosquito cream gel and pay ₹10,000 in composite compensation and litigation costs to a consumer.The commission directed the retail store to discontinue unfair trade practices immediately and restrained it from selling, displaying, or exhibiting expired products for sale.The order follows a complaint filed by Satnam Singh (33) of Manakwal village, who purchased a 25-gram mosquito cream gel alongside other items totaling ₹169 via UPI from the store on July 30, 2025. Upon reaching home, Singh noticed the product label listed an expiry date of May 2025 (05/2025).Singh approached the store and later issued a legal notice on Aug 12, 2025, seeking action, but received no response. He subsequently moved the commission, praying for a full refund with 12% interest, ₹2,00,000 in compensation, and ₹3,500 in litigation expenses.In its written statement, the retail chain argued that retail bills do not carry batch numbers or unique identifiers, claiming the complainant failed to prove the photographed expired item corresponded specifically to that transaction.Rejecting the store’s defence, the commission observed that the retailer could have conveniently disclosed product batch numbers, manufacturing dates, and item descriptions on the invoice, ruling that “the best evidence which was in their power and possession has been withheld for the reasons best known to them.”The commission held that the store was fully conscious that offering an expired item contravenes safety standards and poses human health risks, ordering a full refund of ₹75 within 30 days.
